chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Ismail, from his father who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about an executor of orphans, whose orphans reach adulthood, and he offers them what is theirs, but they refuse him. How should he deal with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return it to them and compel them to take it.'
ai.seo_question: What should an executor do if adult orphans refuse to take their inheritance?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the legal principle of 'ikrah' (compulsion) is applied to financial matters, ensuring that orphans do not remain in a state of suspended ownership. This ruling highlights the executor's duty to actively transfer possession rather than passively waiting, thereby finalizing the orphans' financial independence and preventing indefinite guardianship. The compulsion here is not for their detriment but to fulfill the legal requirement of taking possession, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding orphan wealth management.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Sa’ad Bin Ismail, from his father who said,

‘I asked Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about an executor of orphans, whose orphans become away (adults), but they turn away from taking that which is for them, so they refuse against him. So how should he deal with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should return upon them (the legacy) and compel them upon that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Sa‘d ibn ’Isma‘il from his father who has narrated the following:

“I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the executor of the will under whose supervision the orphans become adults and the executor of the will hands over their assets to them but they refuse to accept. What must he do? He (the Imam) said, ‘They are made to accept their assets.”
